config.title: FUNDA — Permission Gate Directive

intro.title: FUNDA — Permission Gate Directive
intro.body: In this lesson you will build a Permission Gate Directive — a structural directive (*hasPermission) that hides or shows any piece of UI based on the current user's role and permission set. Applied as *hasPermission="'invoice:delete'" on a delete button, the directive checks the AuthService and either renders the template or clears it from the DOM entirely (not just hides it). You will support compound permissions with AND/OR logic via an options input, and implement an *hasRole variant.
intro.usecase: Role-based access control at the UI level is mandatory in HR platforms, financial systems, healthcare portals, and admin dashboards. The structural directive approach centralises RBAC logic and makes templates declarative and self-documenting.

objectives: Create a structural directive that receives a TemplateRef and ViewContainerRef via constructor injection
Implement the @Input setter that triggers a permission check and calls createEmbeddedView() or clear() on the ViewContainerRef
Inject AuthService using the inject() function inside the directive and read the current user's permission array
Support an optional fallback template (@Input as 'appHasPermissionElse') that renders when the permission check fails
Add OR logic support so *hasPermission="['admin','superuser']" shows the element if the user has either role
Ensure the directive re-evaluates when the user's permission set changes (e.g., after assuming a role) by subscribing to an auth observable
Test the directive with a mock AuthService and verify that the template is rendered or cleared based on the permission state
